note: Every figure here is taken from the third-party source named alongside it. Nothing in this file is Cephionix research.

sources.title: Pilot and Technician Outlook 2025–2044
sources.finding: The industry will need 2.4 million new aviation professionals through 2044 — 660,000 pilots, 710,000 maintenance technicians and 1,000,000 cabin crew. Boeing names South Asia and Southeast Asia as the fastest-growing regions for personnel, with staffing demand expected to more than triple. South Asia alone accounts for 141,000 people, including 45,000 pilots.

sources.title: U.S. Civil Airmen Statistics
sources.publisher: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Aeronautical Center, Oklahoma City
sources.finding: The United States had 887,519 active pilots at the end of 2025, including 370,286 active student pilot certificates — up 7.2 per cent on 2024. Student certificates have nearly tripled since 2016, when the figure was 128,501, which is the clearest available measure of how much training volume American flight schools have absorbed in under a decade.

sources.title: Approved Training Organisations (ATOs) and Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011
sources.finding: Every pilot training organisation in Europe must comply with Commission Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011, the Aircrew Regulation, and is approved as an ATO. Notably, the register of approved organisations is maintained by each national aviation authority rather than centrally by EASA, so an operator working across European states deals with several authorities, several registers and several reporting cadences under one common rulebook.

sources.title: Commercial pilot licences issued in India, stated in the Rajya Sabha
sources.publisher: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India (Minister of State Murlidhar Mohol)
sources.finding: India issued 1,331 commercial pilot licences between January and June 2026. Of those, 791 went to cadets trained at Indian flying training organisations and 540 to cadets trained abroad — roughly 41 per cent of the country's new commercial pilots qualified outside India. Full-year figures were 1,652 in 2025, 1,347 in 2024, 1,622 in 2023 and 1,165 in 2022.

sources.title: India's flying training capacity, stated in the Rajya Sabha
sources.publisher: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India
sources.finding: India has 41 DGCA-approved flying training organisations operating across 63 bases with a fleet of more than 400 training aircraft. Under the mandated aircraft-to-instructor-to-student ratio of 1:1:10, that ecosystem can hold roughly 3,500 students at any one time.

sources.title: Annex 19 — Safety Management
sources.finding: Annex 19 consolidated safety management provisions into a single annex and requires service providers to run a Safety Management System built on four pillars: safety policy, risk management, safety assurance and safety promotion. It was the first new ICAO annex in over thirty years. Amendment 2, adopted in 2025, pushes towards a more integrated and proactive approach and becomes applicable in November 2026.

sources.title: Ranking system for DGCA-approved flying training organisations
sources.publisher: Directorate General of Civil Aviation, India
sources.finding: DGCA introduced a ranking system for approved flying training organisations from October 2025, published on a bi-annual cycle. Academies are scored on published parameters, which makes operational discipline and record quality publicly comparable for the first time.
